question.leadin: After this battle, Pheidippides ran approximately 26 miles to Athens to announce a Greek victory.
question.text: Name this 490 BCE battle that lends its name to a very long race.
question.clue: Hippias led Datis and Artaphernes to this battle, where Callimachus disappeared and Miltiades ordered a charge of hoplites.

swap.leadin: A certain city's boule oversaw the process for dealing this kind of punishment, which required 6000 votes to be carried out.
swap.text: Name this kind of punishment,which was dealt to people who were ostracized in ancient Athens.

question.leadin: After the second Persian invasion of Greece, this city-state formed the Delian ("DEE-lee-an") League under the leadership of Cimon ("KY-mun").
question.text: Name this democratic Greek city-state. It fought the Peloponnesian ("peh-luh-puh-NEE-zhuhn") War with Sparta.
question.clue: A bema, or speaker's platform, lies on this city's Pnyx hill.

swap.leadin: -- give the following about classical historians.
swap.text: This Athenian general included Pericles' funeral oration in book two of his History of the Peloponnesian War.
swap.clue: This man included the Melian Dialogue in his major work, which also contains a notoriously difficult-to-translate Funeral Oration.

question.leadin: He created the League of Corinth after defeating Athens at Chaeronea.
question.text: Name this Macedonian king who initiated the invasion of Persia and was assassinated by his bodyguard Pausanias.
question.clue: This leader was killed by a man that Cleitarchus claims had been sexually abused by Attalus.

swap.leadin: The Battle of Pydna marked the end of this formation.
swap.text: Name this military formation of spearmen which was effective in ancient Greece against Persians and other Greeks and involved forming up into a square formation with interlocking shields and charging at the enemy.
swap.clue: Two successive political parties with this name were merged with the Councils of the National-Syndicalist Offensive and the Carlist Party respectively.

question.leadin: While uncovering a "Throne Room" in this city's Palace of Minos, a part time numismatist encountered "lustral basins" that may have been used for purification.
question.text: Name this ancient Minoan city whose 1450 BCE destruction may have been caused by an eruption at Thera.
question.clue: Discoveries near the Dictaean Cave prompted a second attempt to purchase land in Kefala from its Turkish owners; an inability to do so earlier had thwarted the efforts of its original discoverer, Minos Kalokairinos.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a war that lasted from 431 to 404 BCE.
swap.text: The war effectively ended for good after this 405 BCE naval defeat of the Athenians. In this battle, the Spartans under Lysander cut off Athens from the Black Sea's grain exports, causing disaster and famine in the city.
swap.clue: A plan to move the fleet up to Sertos suggested to the losing commanders by Alcibiades was rejected.

question.text: An 1840 blood libel occurred on this Ottoman-ruled island. Philippe Villiers de L'Isle-Adam ("fee-LEEP veel-YAY duh LEEL ah-DOM") and 600 Knights Hospitaller ("hoss-PIT-ah-lur") defended this island for six months in 1522.
question.clue: Previously this polity had been a powerful federal state dominating the commercial traffic of the Eastern Mediterranean through its five ports.

swap.leadin: One event at the Ancient Greek Olympics was a race where men wore the armor and carried the shields used by these soldiers.
swap.text: Identify these Greek foot soldiers who carried a thrusting spear and fought in phalanxes.
swap.clue: Scholars debate if a figurative or literal "push" characterized these people's othismos.

question.leadin: A gold funerary mask found at this site was dubbed the "Mask of Agamemnon" by Heinrich Schliemann.
question.text: Name this archeological site. It names a phase of the Greek bronze age which followed the Minoan civilization and was likely destroyed by the Dorian invasion.
question.clue: A gate topped by two now-headless lions marks the boundary of this site's citadel and separates Grave Circles A and B at this site close to both Argos and Tiryns.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about homosexuality in the Peloponnese in ancient times.
swap.text: At the Battle of Chaeronea, this elite military unit of Theban male lovers were routed by Philip II. During the Corinthian War, this unit was in frequent conflict with Epaminondas.
swap.clue: This group played a major role in winning a decisive victory at the Battle of Leuctra.

question.text: According to linguistic evidence and Greek tradition, this Greek group replaced the fleeing Ionians in the Peloponnesus.
question.clue: Partially because his home city of Herodotus was one of their colonies, Herodotus describes one of their campaigns as the "Return of the Heraclidae".

swap.text: Xenophon's son, Gryllus, died in this battle. Another notable death in this battle was Epaminondas, victor at Leuctra.
swap.clue: At a 418 BC battle at this site, Sparta avenged its defeat at Sphacteria by overcoming an Argos-led alliance of democratic states.

question.text: The siege of Syracuse began after a power struggle resulting from the death of this ninety-year old tyrant, who had managed to keep Syracuse out of the First Punic War by signing a 263 BC treaty with Rome.
question.clue: This tyrant ruled Syracuse until his death in 216 BC, when he was succeeded by his grandson Hieronymus.

swap.leadin: Herodotus wrote that holders of this position had sole jurisdiction over who should marry unbetrothed heiresses and matters concerning public roads.
swap.text: Name this hereditary position held simultaneously by members of the Agiad and Eurypontid families, both of whom claimed descent from Heracles. This office's powers were kept in check by both the gerousia and the ephors.
swap.answerHtml: kings of Sparta [or archagetai; prompt on basileus or kings or monarchs by asking “of what state?”]
swap.clue: These rulers were descended in two lines from the twins Procles and Eurysthenes, and ruled in a diarchy.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about the situation in the Greek world just before the rise of Macedon.
question.text: In this 371 battle, Epaminondas led the Thebans to victory over Cleombrotus and Sparta, beginning the brief pre-eminence of Thebes before the arrival of Philip.
question.clue: The Theban Sacred Band under Epaminondas won a stunning victory against the Spartan phalanx at this 371 BC battle.

swap.leadin: Identify some things about the Peloponnesian War.
swap.text: This battle following earlier battles at Sphacteria and Delium saw the deaths of the generals on both sides when both Cleon and Brasidas were killed.
swap.clue: This all-around disastrous battle that claimed the lives of both commanding generals, Cleon and Brasidas.

question.text: This Corinthian ruler was a member of the Seven Sages and created a ship's' dragway between the Saronic and Corinthian Gulfs called the Diolkos. The Corcyrans, who didn't want his rule, killed his son Lycophron to prevent them from swapping thrones.
question.clue: This man sent three hundred Corcyran nobles to Alyattes, ruler of Lydia, to be made eunuchs.

swap.text: The Chreminodean War was a resounding victory for this Macedonian ruler, whose sister Stratonice married Antiochus I Soter. This son of Demetrius Poliorcetes was later opposed by Aratus of Sicyon and the Achaen League.
swap.answerHtml: Antigonus II Gonatas [accept Antigonus with either sobriquet; prompt on only Antigonus]
